change_request.title: BUG: Add skipna argument to SparseArray.mean
change_request.author: rexmhall09

task.task: Add skipna support to SparseArray.mean and fix missing-value handling in sparse-backed Series.mean.
subtasks: Add a keyword-only skipna: bool = True argument to SparseArray.mean, validate it, and document its behavior. Preserve the default NA-excluding calculation and return the dtype-appropriate NA when skipna=False and missing values are present.
Ensure unsupported dtypes still raise TypeError during mean calculation, even when skipna=False and missing values are present.
Update SparseArray._reduce to pass skipna directly to mean without dropping missing values, preserving dispatch behavior for other reductions.

Add regression tests for default and explicit skipna behavior, including NaN fill values and unsupported object data, and remove mean from the sparse Series reduction expected-failure conditions addressed by this fix.
Add pandas 3.1.0 release notes for both SparseArray.mean accepting skipna and sparse-backed Series.mean respecting skipna=False.

change_request.title: PERF: speed up lexsort_indexer for numeric dtypes
change_request.author: jbrockmendel

task.task: Optimize lexsort_indexer for numeric NumPy arrays to accelerate multi-column DataFrame.sort_values without changing sorting semantics.
subtasks: Add a fast path in pandas/core/sorting.py that bypasses Categorical conversion for NumPy float, signed integer, unsigned integer, and boolean arrays, passing numeric labels directly to np.lexsort while retaining existing handling for other inputs and precomputed codes.

Support descending numeric sorts using negation for floats and bitwise NOT for integers, unsigned integers, and booleans to avoid integer overflow; preserve na_position behavior for floats without mutating input arrays.

Add parameterized tests comparing the numeric fast path against the Categorical-based reference for float64, float32, int64, uint64, and bool across ascending/descending order and both NA positions. Cover float NaNs and descending int64 minimum values explicitly.
Run the existing sorting tests and document the multi-column numeric DataFrame.sort_values performance improvement in the pandas 3.1.0 release notes, referencing issue #15389.

change_request.title: PERF: avoid wasteful array round-trip in loc/iloc setitem with list-of-lists
change_request.author: tuhinsharma121

task.task: Optimize DataFrame.loc and DataFrame.iloc assignment of 2D list-of-lists values to avoid wasteful intermediate NumPy array construction on the split-column setitem path.
subtasks: Detect 2D plain-list values without NumPy conversion, recognizing nonempty lists whose first element is a list or tuple while retaining existing dimensionality checks for other inputs.
Assign list-based values column by column directly, preserving type inference and existing handling of array-like inputs.
Validate every list row against the number of target columns before assignment, raising the existing length-mismatch ValueError for ragged or incorrectly sized values.
Add regression tests for ragged list-of-lists assignments through both loc and iloc, covering shorter rows in either position.

Add an ASV benchmark assigning a large two-column list-of-lists to selected columns of a mixed-dtype DataFrame, and document the performance improvement in the pandas 3.1.0 release notes with reference to #64229.

task.task: Consolidate datetime/timedelta iteration in TimelikeOps and standardize setitem validation on _validate_setitem_value.
subtasks: Move the shared chunked __iter__ implementation and _ITER_CHUNKSIZE = 10_000 into datetimelike.py's TimelikeOps, preserving multidimensional iteration and using the shared constant for both array types.

Add an abstract _iter_convert_chunk hook to TimelikeOps and implement it in DatetimeArray and TimedeltaArray using their existing boxing conversions, preserving datetime timezone and resolution handling. Remove duplicate iterators and unused imports.

Rename _maybe_convert_setitem_value to _validate_setitem_value in ArrowExtensionArray and ArrowStringArray, consolidate StringArray's validation implementation under that name, and update setitem calls, superclass calls, and can_hold_element.

Update DatetimeIndex iteration tests to monkeypatch _ITER_CHUNKSIZE in datetimelike. Run relevant iteration, Arrow/string setitem, Series/DataFrame, and can_hold_element tests, plus mypy on changed files.

change_request.author: jbrockmendel

subtasks: Extend the indexing basics table in doc/source/user_guide/indexing.rst with frame[[colname]] and frame[list_of_colnames], documenting that both return DataFrames.

Explain in the indexing guide that list-like .loc selectors preserve the corresponding axis, while scalar labels reduce it when labels are unique; note that selecting a duplicated column label returns a DataFrame and link to indexing.label.
Add doctest examples to the .loc docstring in pandas/core/indexing.py contrasting df.loc[:, "max_speed"] returning a Series with df.loc[:, ["max_speed"]] returning a DataFrame.

change_request.title: REF: move freq computation from TimedeltaArray arithmetic to TimedeltaIndex
change_request.author: jbrockmendel

task.task: Move frequency computation for TimedeltaArray arithmetic to TimedeltaIndex while preserving Index-level arithmetic behavior.
subtasks: Remove frequency reads and propagation from TimedeltaArray.__mul__, _scalar_divlike_op, __neg__, and __pos__; return results with freq=None.
Implement TimedeltaIndex unary negation and positive overrides that preserve the index name and negate or retain its frequency.
Add Index-level frequency handling for scalar multiplication and division, preserving existing Day conversion, missing-scalar, zero-frequency, and rounding safeguards.
Restore negated frequency for scalar reverse subtraction, including datetime results; preserve Day frequency for datetime reverse subtraction only with timezone-naive or UTC scalars.
Update arithmetic test expectations for array-level negation and reverse subtraction, and validate timedelta array/index, arithmetic, resampling, time-series, and changed-file typing checks.
